p: A visit to Reaseheath Mini Zoo is a short and sweet trip, perfect for younger children and those who'd rather not trek round a vast site. Because it's part of a working college, staff and students bring plenty of enthusiasm and knowledge, so don't be shy about asking questions. Kids who are thinking about a future working with animals may come away inspired, and it's a lovely chance to see the next generation of zookeepers at work.

Once you're done, you're in an excellent part of Cheshire for exploring. Nantwich has a rich history, and it's known for the Battle of Nantwich in 1644, a Civil War clash that's remembered each January with Holly Holy Day, when re-enactors fill the town in period costume. The town's outdoor brine pool, filled with naturally salty water, is a quirky summer favourite. Nantwich Museum, in the town centre, covers everything from salt making to the battle, and it's a nice stop on a wet day.

For something completely different, Hack Green Secret Nuclear Bunker, just south of Nantwich, is a former Cold War government command centre that you can explore, with exhibits about life during the nuclear age. Canal fans will enjoy the Shropshire Union Canal, which passes close to the town on an aqueduct, and the towpath makes a peaceful stroll. Nantwich Riverside, along the banks of the River Weaver, is a pleasant green space for a walk or a picnic. All of that makes it easy to turn a mini zoo visit into a full Cheshire day out.
